transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Recorded: yes (auto)
Attendees: Grace Park (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Anjali Rao (Redwood PM), Sandeep Rao (Aurora Edge), Lina Chen (Aurora Eng), Marcus Blythe (Aurora Solutions), Ravi Patel (Aurora Security)

Summary (auto-generated, rough):
Quick sync to align on marketplace listing artifacts (AWS and Azure), joint reference architecture for private/VPC deployments, packaging options (AMI vs container), billing integration and metering, and security attestations. Agreed next steps for artifacts, demo scaffolding, and co-marketing kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Grace (AE): Okay, hi everyone. Thanks for joining — I think we have about 45 minutes, thanks for accommodating. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Sandeep (Aurora): Hi, Sandeep here. Lina, Marcus, Ravi also on.
[00:17] Grace: Awesome. Diego, do you want to kick us off on the technical checklist?
[00:21] Diego (SE): Yeah, sure. Hi all. We're looking to align on two buckets: marketplace listing requirements (the vendor artifacts, images, metering hooks) and the reference architecture for private deployments — like the VPC template, IAM perms, observability hooks.
[00:38] Lina (Aurora): Quick note — Aurora Edge wants both a SaaS listing and a private offer listing in AWS marketplace. The private offer needs very specific network diagrams and an AMI or container image that can be deployed into our customers' VPCs.
[00:54] Diego: Right, that matches what we've seen. A couple of clarifying questions: do you prefer AMI-based delivery for the private customer, or a container + EKS Helm chart?
[01:05] Marcus (Aurora): Prefer containers, but some of our regulated customers insist on AMIs for air-gapped environments. So we probably need both paths.
[01:15] Grace: That's fine. We'll prepare examples for both. From Redwood side we'll share a container image (ECR) plus a signed AMI pipeline sample.
[01:24] Ravi (Aurora): On security: we need to validate image signing, SBOMs, and supply chain attestations. Also, SOC2 + penetration test artifacts for Redwood's runtime are required.
[01:35] Diego: We can provide SOC2 Type II reports and a vulnerability scan summary. On SBOMs, our build pipeline can emit CycloneDX. Small caveat: some of the product names in our docs get mangled by automatic transcriptions, so I'll send clean artifacts.
[01:49] Sandeep: For the marketplace metering—how will usage be reported? Some of our customers want per-token billing mapped to a SKU inside Marketplace.
[01:58] Grace: Marketplace metering varies by provider. For AWS Marketplace SaaS, we can do Marketplace Metering Service integration and map tokens to usage dimensions. Diego, correct me if I'm wrong on the SKU mapping process.
[02:09] Diego: Yeah, AWS has usage dimensions. We usually instrument at the Redwood proxy layer to emit metering events. For Azure, there's a similar plan-metric mapping but it's more opinionated. We'll share examples.
[02:20] Lina: Do you meter at the request level or token level? Our product needs token-level granularity for downstream chargebacks.
[02:27] Diego: We can emit token counts from the inference runtime. There's a small overhead to counting tokens at high QPS but it's how we preserve accurate billing. We have batching to smooth overhead.
[02:35] Marcus: About the ref-arch: we need a canonical diagram that shows where KV cache lives for multi-tenant vs single-tenant, and how fallback to hosted Redwood works if customer enables hybrid.
[02:47] Anjali (Redwood PM): Yeah, we should include the smart routing piece — show traffic flow for latency-first vs cost-first policy. Also note where observability spans (traces from model invocation down to GPU nodes).
[02:59] Grace: Can we talk timing? What's the internal timeline for Aurora Edge to get artifacts to us?
[03:04] Sandeep: We'd like a public listing draft in 3 weeks, and private offers in 5-6 weeks. That aligns with some co-sell deadlines.
[03:12] Grace: Ok. We'll commit to draft checklist and ref-arch by next Monday (2025-11-10).
[03:20] Ravi: A question on networking — for private deployments, do you recommend a transit VPC or direct peering? Some of our customers mandate no cross-account peering.
[03:28] Diego: Both patterns are supported. The Terraform module will show an encrypted VPC endpoint option (interface endpoints to the Redwood control plane) and an isolated path for air-gapped installs. We'll provide both diagrams.
[03:40] Lina: On deployment automation: will you provide a Helm chart and a Terraform module together, or a single unified repo?
[03:47] Grace: We'll share a repo with both. Diego will own the Terraform + Helm examples.
[03:52] Diego: Yep. For Helm we'll demonstrate values for CPU/GPU nodegroups and how to wire the KV cache to a Redis or local SSD-backed service. Also will show the quantization profile options.
[04:05] Marcus: On quantization — some customers want 4-bit LLMs to save cost, but we need to document perf/latency tradeoffs and supported kernels per instance family.
[04:15] Diego: We'll include a small benchmark matrix — seq length vs latency on T4 vs A10G vs H100-ish instance families. Note: our earlier public doc calls H100 "H-one-hundred" sometimes gets transcribed oddly.
[04:26] Grace: (laughs) noted.
[04:28] [05:00] Sandeep: Another line item — co-selling stock art and logos. We need the Aurora and Redwood logos in specified formats for marketplace pages.
[05:07] Grace: We'll add the logo assets to the checklist. Which marketplace do you want to prioritize — AWS or Azure?
[05:13] Sandeep: Start with AWS, then Azure. GCP is later.
[05:18] Ravi: On the billing front, some enterprise procurement teams require invoicing vs marketplace charges. Can we support both?
[05:25] Anjali: We can support marketplace metering for small customers and direct invoicing for enterprise deals (Dedicated / Private contracts). We'll include notes on pricing models in the joint listing.
[05:36] Lina: A technical nit — how do secrets and keys flow in private installs? We don't want customer keys leaving their VPC.
[05:43] Diego: Keys never leave the customer's control plane in private mode. We integrate with KMS/HSM options. For hosted API we manage the keys but can work with BYOK (bring your own key) via external KMS.
[05:54] Marcus: Observability — we need a primer on the console integration. We want to pull latency/cost per token metrics into our own dashboard. Is there a standard Prometheus export or an API?
[06:04] Diego: Redwood Console exposes traces and a token-level cost API. We also provide a Prometheus exporter and a sample Grafana dashboard. For private installs we'd run the exporter in-cluster and send metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana.
[06:17] Ravi: For security reviews we'll need log retention policies and audit log schemas.
[06:23] Diego: We'll include audit log samples and retention defaults; those are configurable in Private.
[06:28] Grace: Quick check — are there any blockers from Aurora's side to proceed with the Terraform/Helm samples?
[06:33] Lina: Not blockers. We just need ECR access and confirmation on the AMI builder pipeline details.
[06:38] Grace: We'll hand over a basic CI that builds and signs images.
[06:42] [10:00] Sandeep: On the marketplace listing text — we should align on the feature bullets and the value props for enterprise customers. I'll circulate a draft but want Redwood's recommended bullets for performance and cost levers (batching, kv cache, quantization).
[10:14] Anjali: We'll send a prioritized features list and recommended benchmarks. Keep statements conservative — e.g., typical latency numbers with sequence length caveats.
[10:24] Marcus: Integration testing — can we do a joint smoke test in your sandbox? A repo-driven demo that runs an inference and measures end-to-end time?
[10:32] Diego: Yes, we'll provide a demo harness with a small benchmark script. It will show token counting, batching effects, and how routing fallback behaves.
[10:39] Ravi: About legal / procurement — we need to understand the liability model when we resell Redwood as part of our managed offering. Is there an indemnity clause?
[10:48] Grace: Legal teams will need to sync; we'll surface Redwood's standard marketplace MSA and the private deployment addendum. I'll loop in our contracts rep after this call.
[10:58] Sandeep: Fine. Also, do you have a recommended SLA for dedicated capacity? Some of our customers want 99.95% latency SLOs.
[11:07] Diego: For Dedicated we can offer SLA-backed uptimes and latency baselines, but exact numbers depend on committed capacity and instance families. We'll put example SLA language in the draft.
[11:20] [15:00] Lina: A small operational question — how do upgrades work for private installs? Can we orchestrate rolling upgrades, and do you maintain migration scripts?
[15:07] Diego: We support rolling upgrades; the Helm values include a canary deploy option. Migration scripts are part of the repo where needed. For air-gapped customers, upgrades are manual but we provide the checklist and patch bundles.
[15:20] Marcus: Back to telemetry — will the infer logs include prompt redaction? We can't send raw prompts externally for privacy reasons.
[15:28] Diego: Prompts are redacted by default in the telemetry, and there are knobs to keep prompts internal only. We'll include a sample config for privacy-preserving telemetry.
[15:37] Grace: Great. Any unresolved security items?
[15:40] Ravi: Just two: proof of penetration test and detail on key rotation cadence.
[15:46] Diego: We'll attach the pen-test summary and key rotation options (KMS rotation every 90 days or customer-managed).
[15:53] [20:00] Sandeep: One more asks — marketplace images sometimes require a validation step from the market provider. Do you have prior experience submitting images to AWS's procurement validation?
[20:08] Grace: Yes, Redwood has gone through AWS, Azure, and GCP marketplaces. We'll share a playbook — the important bits are image signing, CVE scan report, and the vendor contact info.
[20:19] Lina: For the reference architecture diagram, can Redwood include a minimal single-tenant variant, a multi-tenant variant, and a hybrid where the customer uses Redwood hosted fallback?
[20:29] Anjali: Yea we'll produce three diagrams and annotate the decision gates for security/compliance choices.
[20:35] Marcus: Nice. On the joint solution page in marketplace, do we want to include pricing examples or just point to contact sales?
[20:42] Sandeep: We'll include a starting price band and then say enterprise pricing via contact. Marketplaces prefer a plan with features.
[20:49] [25:00] Diego: Small technical note — when instrumenting metering we usually send events to an internal collector which batches them to the marketplace metering API. We'll provide the event schema.
[25:09] Lina: Please ensure the schema includes a hashed request id and token_count, not full input content.
[25:16] Diego: Yep, hashed ids only.
[25:19] Grace: Ok, we're at about 25 minutes. Let's capture clear action items and owners.
[25:23] [30:00] Sandeep: Also - do you have a sample co-marketing brief? We need to include joint press/launch notes and a list of required approvals.
[30:10] Grace: We'll add a simple co-marketing brief and a timeline. Marketing will reach out for logos and quotes.
[30:18] Marcus: On technical docs — is there a public ref-arch doc we can link to or will this be a bespoke Aurora-Redwood doc?
[30:25] Diego: We'll base it on our public ref-arch and add a partner-specific appendix.
[30:31] Lina: Great. A small gotcha — our internal procurement wants to know if marketplace purchases can enforce region constraints (data residency).
[30:40] Anjali: For Private offers you can restrict region and provide region-specific AMIs or images. We'll document region mapping per marketplace.
[30:49] [35:00] Ravi: Security final: will you enable audit log forwarding to our SIEM? We want Splunk/Datadog connectors in the reference deploy.
[35:09] Diego: Yes, we have connectors and will include sample FluentD/FluentBit config and a small Splunk HTTP Event Collector example.
[35:20] Sandeep: Anything else?
[35:22] Grace: Just reminders on timeline: Redwood to send checklist and artifacts by 11/10, Diego to produce infra examples by 11/14, Aurora to supply ECR/AMI details by 11/17, Ravi to share SOC2/pen test by 11/13. We'll schedule follow-up for 11/18 to review artifacts.
[35:43] Marcus: Sounds good.
[35:45] Lina: One last thing — can we get a sandbox account to run the demo?
[35:49] Diego: Yes, we have a shared sandbox — I'll open an access request and drop creds in the secure channel.
[35:55] [40:00] Grace: Perfect. I'll also add our contracts person to the thread for legal MSA alignment.
[40:06] Sandeep: Thanks everyone, this was useful.
[40:09] Grace: Thanks — we'll follow up with the checklist and a calendar invite for the 11/18 artifact review.
[40:15] (meeting ends)
